subject: Tonga
note: Cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary): 2022 Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai eruption and tsunami, and Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai. Only stated distances, heights and dates are used. Sound distances are the page's approximate figures ('roughly', 'approximately', 'more than'). The page gives two island-area/count descriptions and a USGS magnitude that a script does not use. No before-and-after outline of the islands is drawn (the page says the 2022 eruption reduced their size but the pinned data holds no outline of them): the map shows today's coast with figures and labels.

claims.text: Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai is a submarine volcano in the Tongan archipelago in the southern Pacific Ocean, 65 kilometres (40 mi) north of Tongatapu, the country's main island.
The eruption reached a very large and powerful climax on 15 January 2022; the eruption column from the Plinian eruption rose 58 km (36 mi) into the mesosphere.
It generated the largest atmospheric explosion recorded by modern instrumentation, far larger than any 20th-century volcanic event or nuclear bomb test.
The explosion was heard in Samoa, roughly 840 km (520 mi) away.
The eruption was heard more than 2,000 km (1,200 mi) away in New Zealand, where the sound arrived two hours later.
A series of bangs were heard in and around Anchorage, Alaska, approximately 9,300 km (5,800 mi) away from the volcano, lasting about 30 minutes.
Booms were heard as far away as Yukon in Canada, 9,700 km (6,000 mi) away.

The eruption produced a volcanic tsunami that affected Tonga, Fiji, American Samoa, Samoa, Vanuatu, New Zealand, Japan, the United States, the Russian Far East, Chile and Peru; at least four people were killed in Tonga by waves up to 20 m (66 ft) high.
Tsunami waves with run-up heights up to 45 m (148 ft) struck the uninhabited island of Tofua.
The volcano rises around 2,000 m from the seafloor, and the only major above-water parts are the twin uninhabited islands of Hunga Tonga and Hunga Ha'apai.
